name: Ab Scissors
description: A lying core exercise where the legs cross over each other in a scissor motion while held off the floor, working the lower abs and hip flexors.
instructions: Lie on your back with your hands under your glutes and your lower back pressed into the floor.
Lift both legs a few inches off the floor, keeping them straight.
Cross one leg over the other, then switch, alternating in a smooth scissor motion.
Keep your lower back flat and breathe steadily; stop if your back starts to arch.

name: Ab Wheel
description: An anti-extension core exercise: rolling a wheel forward and back from the knees trains the abs to keep the spine from sagging.
instructions: Kneel on a mat and hold the ab wheel under your shoulders with straight arms.
Brace your abs and tuck your pelvis slightly so your back stays flat.
Roll the wheel forward slowly, extending your body as far as you can without letting your hips sag.
Pull the wheel back toward your knees using your abs, not your arms.

name: Alternating Bicep Curl
description: A dumbbell curl performed one arm at a time, letting you focus on each biceps and keep strict form.
instructions: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand, arms extended and palms facing forward.
Keeping your elbow pinned to your side, curl one dumbbell up toward your shoulder.
Squeeze the biceps at the top, then lower it under control to full extension.
Repeat with the other arm and keep alternating; avoid swinging your torso.

name: Alternating Hammer Curl
description: A curl with a neutral grip (palms facing each other), done one arm at a time, that targets the brachialis, brachioradialis and biceps.
instructions: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing your body.
Curl one dumbbell up while keeping your palm facing in and your elbow fixed at your side.
Lower it slowly to full extension.
Alternate arms on each repetition without swinging.

name: Arnold Press (Seated)
description: A seated dumbbell shoulder press that rotates the palms during the press, working all three heads of the deltoids with an emphasis on the front.
instructions: Sit on a bench with back support, holding the dumbbells in front of your shoulders with your palms facing you.
Press the dumbbells overhead while rotating your palms to face forward.
Finish with your arms extended above your head without locking the elbows hard.
Reverse the rotation as you lower back to the start position.

name: Arnold Press (Standing)
description: A standing version of the Arnold press, which adds core stabilisation to the rotating shoulder press.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding the dumbbells in front of your shoulders with your palms facing you.
Brace your core and glutes so your lower back does not arch.
Press overhead while rotating your palms to face forward.
Lower under control while rotating back to the start position.

name: Assisted Pistol Squats
description: A single-leg squat performed while holding a support, a progression toward the full pistol squat that builds leg strength and balance.
instructions: Stand on one leg next to a sturdy support (pole, rack or TRX) and hold it lightly.
Extend the other leg in front of you.
Sit back and down on the standing leg as low as you can control, keeping the heel on the floor.
Push through the whole foot to stand back up, using the support only as much as needed.

name: Back Extension (Machine)
description: A hip and spine extension movement that strengthens the lower back, glutes and hamstrings.
instructions: Sit in the back extension machine with the pad against your upper back and your feet secured, then select the weight.
Lower your torso toward the floor by hinging at the hips, keeping your back neutral.
Raise your torso until your body forms a straight line, squeezing your glutes and lower back.
Avoid hyperextending past a straight line, then lower slowly.

name: Back Extension (Bodyweight)
description: A hip and spine extension movement that strengthens the lower back, glutes and hamstrings.
instructions: Set the pad of a hyperextension bench just below your hips, lock your feet in and cross your arms over your chest.
Lower your torso toward the floor by hinging at the hips, keeping your back neutral.
Raise your torso until your body forms a straight line, squeezing your glutes and lower back.
Avoid hyperextending past a straight line, then lower slowly.

name: Back Extension (Weighted)
description: A back extension performed while holding a weight plate or dumbbell, to add load for the lower back, glutes and hamstrings.
instructions: Set the pad of a hyperextension bench just below your hips and lock your feet in.
Hold a weight plate or dumbbell against your chest.
Lower your torso by hinging at the hips, keeping your back neutral.
Raise your torso until your body is in a straight line, without hyperextending.

name: Baesyan Curl (Cable)
description: Also called the Bayesian curl: a curl performed with the arm behind the torso, which stretches the long head of the biceps under load.
instructions: Set a cable pulley low, grab the handle with one hand and step forward so that your arm is pulled slightly behind your body.
Curl the handle toward your shoulder while keeping your elbow behind your torso.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly to a full stretch.
Complete all repetitions on one side before switching.

name: Baesyan Curl (Dumbbell)
description: Also called the Bayesian curl: a curl performed with the arm behind the torso, which stretches the long head of the biceps under load.
instructions: Lie back on an incline bench or lean forward slightly so that the arm holding the dumbbell hangs behind your torso.
Curl the handle toward your shoulder while keeping your elbow behind your torso.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly to a full stretch.
Complete all repetitions on one side before switching.

name: Ball Slams
description: An explosive full-body exercise where a slam ball is lifted overhead and thrown into the floor, building power and conditioning.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a slam ball at your chest.
Lift the ball overhead, rising onto the balls of your feet.
Slam the ball into the floor in front of you as hard as you can, hinging at the hips.
Squat down to pick the ball up and repeat.

name: Battle Ropes
description: A conditioning exercise using heavy ropes anchored to a point, creating waves to train the shoulders, arms, core and cardiovascular system.
instructions: Stand facing the anchor, feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, holding one rope end in each hand.
Brace your core and keep your chest up.
Move your arms up and down quickly, alternately or together, to create waves along the ropes.
Keep the waves going for the planned time while breathing steadily.

name: Behind the Back Bicep Wrist Curl (Barbell)
description: A forearm exercise where the weight is held behind the body and curled with the wrists, targeting the wrist flexors.
instructions: Stand holding a barbell behind your back with an overhand grip, palms facing back, arms extended.
Let the bar roll down to your fingertips, then curl it back up by flexing your wrists.
Squeeze at the top and lower under control.
Keep your arms still: only the wrists and fingers should move.

name: Behind the Back Bicep Wrist Curl (Cable)
description: A forearm exercise where the weight is held behind the body and curled with the wrists, targeting the wrist flexors.
instructions: Stand with your back to a low pulley, holding a straight bar behind your back with your palms facing back.
Let the bar roll down to your fingertips, then curl it back up by flexing your wrists.
Squeeze at the top and lower under control.
Keep your arms still: only the wrists and fingers should move.

name: Belt Squat
description: A squat where the load hangs from a hip belt instead of resting on the spine, training the quads and glutes with very little back loading.
instructions: Attach the belt around your hips and stand on the platform with feet shoulder-width apart.
Release the safety and hold the handles for balance.
Squat down by bending your knees and hips, keeping your chest up.
Drive through your feet to stand back up.

name: Bench Dip
description: A bodyweight triceps exercise performed with the hands on a bench behind you.
instructions: Sit on the edge of a bench, hands next to your hips, fingers pointing forward.
Slide your hips off the bench and extend your legs in front of you.
Lower your body by bending your elbows to about 90 degrees, keeping your back close to the bench.
Press through your palms to straighten your arms.

name: Bench Press (Cable)
description: The classic horizontal press for the chest, front deltoids and triceps.
instructions: Place a flat bench between two low cable pulleys and lie on it holding one handle in each hand at chest level.
Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor and your shoulder blades pulled back and down.
Lower the weight under control to mid-chest level, keeping your elbows at roughly 45 degrees from your torso.
Press back up until your arms are extended, without bouncing off the chest.

name: Bench Press (Dumbbell)
description: The classic horizontal press for the chest, front deltoids and triceps.
instructions: Sit on the bench with the dumbbells on your thighs, then lie back and bring them to chest level.
Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor and your shoulder blades pulled back and down.
Lower the weight under control to mid-chest level, keeping your elbows at roughly 45 degrees from your torso.
Press back up until your arms are extended, without bouncing off the chest.

name: Bench Press (Smith Machine)
description: The classic horizontal press for the chest, front deltoids and triceps.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench under a Smith machine so the bar is above your mid-chest, grip it slightly wider than your shoulders and unhook it.
Lie on a flat bench with your feet flat on the floor and your shoulder blades pulled back and down.
Lower the weight under control to mid-chest level, keeping your elbows at roughly 45 degrees from your torso.
Press back up until your arms are extended, without bouncing off the chest.

name: Bench Press - Close Grip
description: A bench press with the hands about shoulder-width apart, shifting the work toward the triceps.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench and grip the bar with your hands about shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the bar and hold it above your chest with straight arms.
Lower the bar to your lower chest, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Press back up, focusing on extending the elbows.

name: Bench Press - Wide Grip
description: A bench press with a grip wider than shoulder width, emphasising the chest over the triceps.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench and grip the bar noticeably wider than shoulder width.
Pull your shoulder blades back and unrack the bar.
Lower the bar under control to your mid-chest.
Press back up without letting your shoulders roll forward.

name: Bench Press (Decline, Barbell)
description: A bench press performed on a decline bench, emphasising the lower part of the chest.
instructions: Secure your legs at the end of a decline bench and lie back.
Unrack the barbell with a grip slightly wider than your shoulders and hold it above your lower chest.
Lower the weight to your lower chest under control.
Press back up until your arms are extended.

name: Bench Press (Decline, Dumbbell)
description: A bench press performed on a decline bench, emphasising the lower part of the chest.
instructions: Secure your legs at the end of a decline bench and lie back.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand above your lower chest, palms facing forward.
Lower the weight to your lower chest under control.
Press back up until your arms are extended.

name: Bench Press (Decline, Smith Machine)
description: A bench press performed on a decline bench, emphasising the lower part of the chest.
instructions: Secure your legs at the end of a decline bench and lie back.
Check that the Smith machine bar lines up with your lower chest, grip it slightly wider than your shoulders and unhook it.
Lower the weight to your lower chest under control.
Press back up until your arms are extended.

name: Bench Press (Incline, Barbell)
description: A bench press on an incline bench (about 30 to 45 degrees), emphasising the upper chest and front deltoids.
instructions: Set the bench to an incline of about 30 to 45 degrees and lie back with your feet flat.
Unrack the barbell with a grip slightly wider than your shoulders.
Lower the weight to your upper chest, elbows at roughly 45 degrees from your torso.
Press back up and slightly back over your shoulders.

name: Bench Press (Incline, Dumbbell)
description: A bench press on an incline bench (about 30 to 45 degrees), emphasising the upper chest and front deltoids.
instructions: Set the bench to an incline of about 30 to 45 degrees and lie back with your feet flat.
Bring the dumbbells to your shoulders, palms facing forward.
Lower the weight to your upper chest, elbows at roughly 45 degrees from your torso.
Press back up and slightly back over your shoulders.

name: Bench Press (Incline, Smith Machine)
description: A bench press on an incline bench (about 30 to 45 degrees), emphasising the upper chest and front deltoids.
instructions: Set the bench to an incline of about 30 to 45 degrees and lie back with your feet flat.
Check that the Smith machine bar lines up with your upper chest, grip it slightly wider than your shoulders and unhook it.
Lower the weight to your upper chest, elbows at roughly 45 degrees from your torso.
Press back up and slightly back over your shoulders.

name: Bent Over Row (Band)
description: A hinged rowing movement that builds the lats, rhomboids, traps and rear deltoids.
instructions: Stand on the middle of the band and hold one end in each hand.
Hinge at the hips until your torso is between parallel and 45 degrees to the floor, back flat and knees slightly bent.
Pull the weight toward your lower ribs, driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades.
Lower under control to full arm extension without rounding your back.

name: Bent Over Row (Barbell)
description: A hinged rowing movement that builds the lats, rhomboids, traps and rear deltoids.
instructions: Hold the barbell with an overhand grip slightly wider than your shoulders.
Hinge at the hips until your torso is between parallel and 45 degrees to the floor, back flat and knees slightly bent.
Pull the weight toward your lower ribs, driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades.
Lower under control to full arm extension without rounding your back.

name: Bent Over Row (Dumbbell)
description: A hinged rowing movement that builds the lats, rhomboids, traps and rear deltoids.
instructions: Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing your body.
Hinge at the hips until your torso is between parallel and 45 degrees to the floor, back flat and knees slightly bent.
Pull the weight toward your lower ribs, driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades.
Lower under control to full arm extension without rounding your back.

name: Bicep Curl (Band)
description: The basic elbow flexion exercise for the biceps.
instructions: Stand on the middle of the band and hold one end in each hand, palms facing forward.
Stand tall with your elbows close to your sides.
Curl the weight up toward your shoulders without moving your upper arms.
Squeeze the biceps at the top, then lower slowly to full extension.
Avoid swinging your torso to lift the weight.

name: Bicep Curl (Barbell)
description: The basic elbow flexion exercise for the biceps.
instructions: Hold a barbell with an underhand grip at shoulder width, arms extended.
Stand tall with your elbows close to your sides.
Curl the weight up toward your shoulders without moving your upper arms.
Squeeze the biceps at the top, then lower slowly to full extension.
Avoid swinging your torso to lift the weight.

name: Bicep Curl (Cable)
description: The basic elbow flexion exercise for the biceps.
instructions: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley and hold it with an underhand grip.
Stand tall with your elbows close to your sides.
Curl the weight up toward your shoulders without moving your upper arms.
Squeeze the biceps at the top, then lower slowly to full extension.
Avoid swinging your torso to lift the weight.

name: Bicep Curl (Kettlebell)
description: The basic elbow flexion exercise for the biceps.
instructions: Hold a kettlebell by the handle in each hand, or one kettlebell by the horns with both hands.
Stand tall with your elbows close to your sides.
Curl the weight up toward your shoulders without moving your upper arms.
Squeeze the biceps at the top, then lower slowly to full extension.
Avoid swinging your torso to lift the weight.

name: Bicep Curl (Machine)
description: The basic elbow flexion exercise for the biceps.
instructions: Sit at the curl machine with your upper arms on the pad and grip the handles.
Stand tall with your elbows close to your sides.
Curl the weight up toward your shoulders without moving your upper arms.
Squeeze the biceps at the top, then lower slowly to full extension.
Avoid swinging your torso to lift the weight.

name: Bicep Curl (Plate Loaded)
description: The basic elbow flexion exercise for the biceps.
instructions: Sit at the plate-loaded curl machine with your upper arms on the pad and grip the handles.
Stand tall with your elbows close to your sides.
Curl the weight up toward your shoulders without moving your upper arms.
Squeeze the biceps at the top, then lower slowly to full extension.
Avoid swinging your torso to lift the weight.

name: Bicep Curl (EZ Bar)
description: A biceps curl with an EZ bar, whose angled grip is easier on the wrists than a straight bar.
instructions: Hold the angled grips of the EZ bar with your palms facing up, arms extended.
Curl the bar toward your shoulders, keeping your elbows at your sides.
Squeeze at the top, then lower under control.

name: Bicep Curl (EZ Bar, Cable)
description: A biceps curl with an EZ bar, whose angled grip is easier on the wrists than a straight bar.
instructions: Attach an EZ bar to a low pulley and stand facing the machine.
Hold the angled grips of the EZ bar with your palms facing up, arms extended.
Curl the bar toward your shoulders, keeping your elbows at your sides.
Squeeze at the top, then lower under control.

name: Bicep Curl (Incline, Cable)
description: A curl performed lying back on an incline bench, which puts the biceps in a stretched position at the bottom.
instructions: Place the bench in front of a low pulley (or between two) so the cables pull your arms down and slightly back.
Set a bench to about 45 to 60 degrees and lie back with your arms hanging straight down.
Curl the weight up without bringing your elbows forward.
Lower slowly to a full stretch at the bottom.

name: Bicep Curl (Incline, Dumbbell)
description: A curl performed lying back on an incline bench, which puts the biceps in a stretched position at the bottom.
instructions: Set a bench to about 45 to 60 degrees and lie back with your arms hanging straight down.
Curl the weight up without bringing your elbows forward.
Lower slowly to a full stretch at the bottom.

name: Bicep Curl (Seated)
description: A dumbbell curl performed seated, which removes the leg drive and keeps the work on the biceps.
instructions: Sit on the end of a bench, back straight, a dumbbell in each hand with your arms extended.
Curl the dumbbells toward your shoulders, rotating your palms up.
Squeeze at the top, then lower under control.

name: Bicep Curl (Standing, Dumbbell)
description: A standing biceps curl with free weights.
instructions: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing forward.
Stand tall, feet hip-width apart, elbows close to your sides.
Curl the weight toward your shoulders without swinging.
Lower slowly until your arms are fully extended.

name: Bicep Curl (Standing, Barbell)
description: A standing biceps curl with free weights.
instructions: Hold a barbell with an underhand grip at shoulder width.
Stand tall, feet hip-width apart, elbows close to your sides.
Curl the weight toward your shoulders without swinging.
Lower slowly until your arms are fully extended.

name: Bicycle Crunch
description: A crunch with a pedalling leg motion and torso rotation, working the upper abs and obliques.
instructions: Lie on your back with your hands lightly behind your head and your legs raised, knees bent.
Bring one knee toward your chest while rotating the opposite elbow toward it.
Extend that leg as you switch sides in a pedalling motion.
Keep your lower back pressed into the floor and do not pull on your neck.

name: Bicycle Crunch Raised Legs
description: A harder bicycle crunch where the legs stay raised throughout, increasing the work of the lower abs.
instructions: Lie on your back, hands behind your head, and lift both legs so your thighs are vertical.
Lift your shoulders off the floor and keep them up.
Rotate one elbow toward the opposite knee while extending the other leg forward.
Switch sides in a slow pedalling motion without letting your feet touch the floor.

name: Bird Dog
description: A low-impact stability exercise on all fours that strengthens the lower back, glutes and deep core muscles.
instructions: Start on your hands and knees, hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
Brace your core and keep your back flat.
Extend one arm forward and the opposite leg back until both are in line with your torso.
Hold for a moment, return to the start and switch sides.

name: Box Jump
description: A plyometric jump onto a box that develops explosive leg power.
instructions: Stand facing a sturdy box at a comfortable distance, feet hip-width apart.
Dip into a quarter squat and swing your arms back.
Jump explosively onto the box, landing softly with both feet and bent knees.
Stand up fully on the box, then step down rather than jumping down.

name: Box Squat (Barbell)
description: A squat where you sit back onto a box at the bottom, teaching depth and hip drive.
instructions: Place a box behind you at a height that puts your thighs around parallel when seated.
Set the bar on your upper back in a rack, unrack it and step back in front of the box.
Sit back onto the box under control, keeping your shins near vertical.
Pause briefly on the box without relaxing your core.
Drive through your heels to stand back up.

name: Box Squat (Smith Machine)
description: A squat where you sit back onto a box at the bottom, teaching depth and hip drive.
instructions: Place a box behind you at a height that puts your thighs around parallel when seated.
Place the Smith machine bar on your upper back and unhook it.
Sit back onto the box under control, keeping your shins near vertical.
Pause briefly on the box without relaxing your core.
Drive through your heels to stand back up.

name: Boxing
description: A combat sport workout (bag work, pads or shadow boxing) that trains conditioning, coordination and upper-body endurance.
instructions: Warm up with shadow boxing and light footwork.
Stand in your guard: feet staggered, knees soft, hands up protecting your face.
Throw combinations with rotation from your hips, returning your hands to the guard after each punch.
Work in timed rounds with short rests and keep breathing out on each punch.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
description: A single-leg squat with the rear foot raised on a bench, building quads, glutes and balance.
instructions: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and stand about two steps in front of a bench.
Place the top of your rear foot on the bench.
Lower your hips until your front thigh is about parallel to the floor, keeping your torso upright.
Drive through the front heel to stand back up; complete all reps before switching legs.

name: Burpee
description: A full-body conditioning exercise chaining a squat, a plank, a push-up and a jump.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Squat down and place your hands on the floor in front of you.
Jump your feet back into a plank and do a push-up.
Jump your feet back toward your hands, then jump up with your arms overhead.

name: Butterfly
description: A pec deck machine fly that isolates the chest with a guided path.
instructions: Adjust the seat so the handles are at chest height and sit with your back against the pad.
Grip the handles with your arms open and a slight bend in your elbows.
Bring the handles together in front of your chest, squeezing your pecs.
Return slowly until you feel a stretch across your chest.

name: Calf Extension (Machine)
description: A calf exercise on a leg press type machine, where the feet push the platform by extending the ankles.
instructions: Sit in the machine and place the balls of your feet on the bottom edge of the platform.
Extend your legs without locking your knees.
Push the platform by pointing your toes as far as possible.
Lower slowly until you feel a stretch in your calves.

name: Calf Extension (Plate Loaded)
description: A calf exercise on a leg press type machine, where the feet push the platform by extending the ankles.
instructions: Sit in the machine and place the balls of your feet on the bottom edge of the platform.
Extend your legs without locking your knees.
Push the platform by pointing your toes as far as possible.
Lower slowly until you feel a stretch in your calves.

name: Calf Press (Machine)
description: A calf raise performed on a calf press or leg press machine, targeting the gastrocnemius and soleus.
instructions: Sit in the machine with the balls of your feet on the platform and your heels hanging off.
Push the platform by extending your ankles as far as possible.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly into a full stretch.

name: Calf Press (Plate Loaded)
description: A calf raise performed on a calf press or leg press machine, targeting the gastrocnemius and soleus.
instructions: Sit in the machine with the balls of your feet on the platform and your heels hanging off.
Push the platform by extending your ankles as far as possible.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly into a full stretch.

name: Calf Raise (Barbell)
description: A standing raise onto the toes that builds the calves.
instructions: Place a barbell on your upper back as for a squat.
Stand with the balls of your feet on a raised edge and your heels hanging off.
Rise onto your toes as high as possible, keeping your knees straight but not locked.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly until you feel a stretch in your calves.

name: Calf Raise (Dumbbell)
description: A standing raise onto the toes that builds the calves.
instructions: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, or one dumbbell and a support with the other hand.
Stand with the balls of your feet on a raised edge and your heels hanging off.
Rise onto your toes as high as possible, keeping your knees straight but not locked.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly until you feel a stretch in your calves.

name: Calf Raise (Machine)
description: A standing raise onto the toes that builds the calves.
instructions: Step under the shoulder pads of the standing calf machine.
Stand with the balls of your feet on a raised edge and your heels hanging off.
Rise onto your toes as high as possible, keeping your knees straight but not locked.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly until you feel a stretch in your calves.

name: Calf Raise (Plate Loaded)
description: A standing raise onto the toes that builds the calves.
instructions: Step under the shoulder pads of the plate-loaded calf machine.
Stand with the balls of your feet on a raised edge and your heels hanging off.
Rise onto your toes as high as possible, keeping your knees straight but not locked.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly until you feel a stretch in your calves.

name: Calf Raise (Smith Machine)
description: A standing raise onto the toes that builds the calves.
instructions: Place the Smith machine bar on your upper back and unhook it.
Stand with the balls of your feet on a raised edge and your heels hanging off.
Rise onto your toes as high as possible, keeping your knees straight but not locked.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly until you feel a stretch in your calves.

name: Calf Raise (Bodyweight)
description: A standing raise onto the toes that builds the calves.
instructions: Hold a wall or rail lightly for balance.
Stand with the balls of your feet on a raised edge and your heels hanging off.
Rise onto your toes as high as possible, keeping your knees straight but not locked.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly until you feel a stretch in your calves.

name: Calf Raise (Seated, Machine)
description: A calf raise performed seated with bent knees, which emphasises the soleus.
instructions: Sit at the machine with the balls of your feet on the platform and the pad resting on your lower thighs.
Release the safety lever.
Raise your heels as high as possible, pause, then lower slowly into a full stretch.

name: Calf Raise (Seated, Plate Loaded)
description: A calf raise performed seated with bent knees, which emphasises the soleus.
instructions: Sit at the machine with the balls of your feet on the platform and the pad resting on your lower thighs.
Release the safety lever.
Raise your heels as high as possible, pause, then lower slowly into a full stretch.

name: Chest Dip (Assisted)
description: A dip on an assisted machine where a counterweight reduces the load, to build toward bodyweight dips.
instructions: Select the assistance weight, kneel or stand on the platform and grip the handles.
Lean your torso slightly forward to bias the chest.
Lower until your shoulders are slightly below your elbows.
Press back up to straight arms.

name: Chest Dip (Bodyweight)
description: A dip on parallel bars with the torso leaning forward to emphasise the lower chest.
instructions: Support yourself on parallel bars with straight arms.
Lean your torso forward and let your elbows flare slightly.
Lower until you feel a stretch in your chest and your shoulders are about level with your elbows.
Press back up to straight arms.

name: Chest Dip (Weighted)
description: A chest dip with extra weight attached to a dip belt or held between the legs.
instructions: Attach a weight to a dip belt (or hold a dumbbell between your feet) and support yourself on the bars.
Lean your torso forward.
Lower until your shoulders are about level with your elbows.
Press back up to straight arms without swinging.

name: Chest Fly (Band)
description: An isolation exercise for the chest where the arms move in a wide arc with a slight bend at the elbows.
instructions: Anchor the band behind you at chest height and hold one end in each hand.
Start with your arms open wide and a slight, fixed bend in your elbows.
Bring your hands together in front of your chest in a hugging motion.
Squeeze your chest, then return slowly until you feel a stretch.

name: Chest Fly (Cable)
description: An isolation exercise for the chest where the arms move in a wide arc with a slight bend at the elbows.
instructions: Set both pulleys at chest height, hold one handle in each hand and step forward.
Start with your arms open wide and a slight, fixed bend in your elbows.
Bring your hands together in front of your chest in a hugging motion.
Squeeze your chest, then return slowly until you feel a stretch.

name: Chest Fly (Dumbbell)
description: An isolation exercise for the chest where the arms move in a wide arc with a slight bend at the elbows.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench holding the dumbbells above your chest, palms facing each other.
Start with your arms open wide and a slight, fixed bend in your elbows.
Bring your hands together in front of your chest in a hugging motion.
Squeeze your chest, then return slowly until you feel a stretch.

name: Chest Fly (Machine)
description: An isolation exercise for the chest where the arms move in a wide arc with a slight bend at the elbows.
instructions: Sit at the fly machine with your back against the pad and grip the handles.
Start with your arms open wide and a slight, fixed bend in your elbows.
Bring your hands together in front of your chest in a hugging motion.
Squeeze your chest, then return slowly until you feel a stretch.

name: Chest Fly (Plate Loaded)
description: An isolation exercise for the chest where the arms move in a wide arc with a slight bend at the elbows.
instructions: Sit at the plate-loaded fly machine with your back against the pad and grip the handles.
Start with your arms open wide and a slight, fixed bend in your elbows.
Bring your hands together in front of your chest in a hugging motion.
Squeeze your chest, then return slowly until you feel a stretch.

name: Chest Fly (Decline)
description: A dumbbell fly on a decline bench, emphasising the lower chest.
instructions: Lie on a decline bench with your legs secured, dumbbells above your chest and palms facing each other.
Open your arms in a wide arc with a slight bend in the elbows.
Lower until you feel a stretch, then bring the dumbbells back together.

name: Chest Fly (High to Low)
description: A cable fly that moves from high pulleys down toward the hips, emphasising the lower chest.
instructions: Set both pulleys high, hold one handle in each hand and step forward into a staggered stance.
With a slight bend in your elbows, bring the handles down and together in front of your hips.
Squeeze, then return slowly to the start.

name: Chest Fly (Incline)
description: A dumbbell fly on an incline bench, emphasising the upper chest.
instructions: Lie on a bench inclined to about 30 degrees, dumbbells above your chest and palms facing each other.
Open your arms in a wide arc with a slight bend in the elbows.
Lower until you feel a stretch, then bring the dumbbells back together above your upper chest.

name: Chest Fly (Low to High)
description: A cable fly that moves from low pulleys up toward the face, emphasising the upper chest.
instructions: Set both pulleys low, hold one handle in each hand and step forward.
With a slight bend in your elbows, bring the handles up and together in front of your upper chest.
Squeeze, then return slowly to the start.

name: Chest Fly (Seated)
description: A cable fly performed seated, which removes the need to stabilise with the legs.
instructions: Place a bench between two pulleys set at chest height and sit with your back straight.
Hold one handle in each hand with your arms open and elbows slightly bent.
Bring the handles together in front of your chest, then return slowly.

name: Chest Fly (Suspension)
description: A fly performed with suspension straps (TRX), where body angle sets the difficulty.
instructions: Hold the handles in front of your chest and lean forward with your body straight.
Open your arms wide while lowering your chest between the handles, keeping a slight elbow bend.
Pull the handles back together to return to the start, keeping your core tight.

name: Chest Press (Band)
description: A guided horizontal press for the chest, shoulders and triceps.
instructions: Anchor the band behind you at chest height, hold one end in each hand and step forward until there is tension.
Push forward until your arms are extended without locking your elbows.
Return slowly until the handles are level with your chest.

name: Chest Press (Machine)
description: A guided horizontal press for the chest, shoulders and triceps.
instructions: Adjust the seat so the handles are at mid-chest height and sit with your back against the pad.
Push forward until your arms are extended without locking your elbows.
Return slowly until the handles are level with your chest.

name: Chest Press (Plate Loaded)
description: A guided horizontal press for the chest, shoulders and triceps.
instructions: Adjust the seat so the handles are at mid-chest height and sit with your back against the pad.
Push forward until your arms are extended without locking your elbows.
Return slowly until the handles are level with your chest.

name: Chest Press (Decline, Machine)
description: A decline press on a machine, emphasising the lower chest.
instructions: Adjust the seat and sit with your back against the pad, handles at lower chest height.
Press the handles forward and down until your arms are extended.
Return slowly to the start.

name: Chest Press (Decline, Plate Loaded)
description: A decline press on a machine, emphasising the lower chest.
instructions: Adjust the seat and sit with your back against the pad, handles at lower chest height.
Press the handles forward and down until your arms are extended.
Return slowly to the start.

name: Chest Press (Incline, Machine)
description: An incline press on a machine, emphasising the upper chest.
instructions: Adjust the seat so the handles are at upper chest height and sit with your back against the pad.
Press the handles forward and up until your arms are extended.
Return slowly to the start.

name: Chest Press (Incline, Plate Loaded)
description: An incline press on a machine, emphasising the upper chest.
instructions: Adjust the seat so the handles are at upper chest height and sit with your back against the pad.
Press the handles forward and up until your arms are extended.
Return slowly to the start.

name: Chest Supported Incline Row
description: A dumbbell row lying face down on an incline bench, which removes lower-back strain and isolates the back muscles.
instructions: Lie face down on a bench inclined to about 30 to 45 degrees, a dumbbell in each hand hanging down.
Row the dumbbells toward your hips, driving your elbows back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together, then lower under control.

name: Chest Supported Reverse Fly
description: A reverse fly lying face down on an incline bench, isolating the rear deltoids and upper back.
instructions: Lie face down on an incline bench with a light dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging down.
With a slight bend in your elbows, raise your arms out to the sides until they are level with your body.
Squeeze your shoulder blades, then lower slowly.

name: Chest Supported Y Raise
description: A raise lying face down on an incline bench where the arms travel in a Y shape, working the lower traps and rear shoulders.
instructions: Lie face down on an incline bench with a light dumbbell in each hand, thumbs pointing up.
Raise your arms forward and out to form a Y with your body.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly; keep the weight light and the movement strict.

name: Chin Up
description: A vertical pull with an underhand grip that works the lats and biceps.
instructions: Hang from a bar with your palms facing you, hands about shoulder-width apart.
Pull your shoulder blades down, then pull your chest toward the bar.
Go up until your chin is over the bar.
Lower slowly to a full hang.

name: Chin Up (Assisted)
description: A chin-up on an assisted machine, where a counterweight reduces the load.
instructions: Select the assistance weight and kneel or stand on the platform.
Grip the handles with your palms facing you.
Pull until your chin is above the handles, then lower slowly to full extension.

name: Chin Up (Weigthed)
description: A chin-up with extra weight attached to a belt or held between the legs.
instructions: Attach a weight to a dip belt (or hold a dumbbell between your feet).
Hang from a bar with your palms facing you, hands about shoulder-width apart.
Pull until your chin is over the bar, then lower slowly to a full hang.

name: Clap Push Ups
description: An explosive push-up where the hands leave the floor to clap, building upper-body power.
instructions: Start in a push-up position with your body in a straight line.
Lower your chest toward the floor.
Push up explosively so your hands leave the floor, clap quickly, and land with soft elbows.
Go straight into the next repetition.

name: Climbing
description: Rock or indoor climbing, which trains grip, back, arms and core while improving coordination.
instructions: Warm up your fingers, shoulders and hips before climbing.
Keep your weight over your feet and use your legs to push you up.
Keep your arms as straight as possible to save grip strength.
Rest between routes and stop before your grip is completely exhausted.

name: Concentration Curl
description: A seated single-arm curl with the elbow braced against the thigh, isolating the biceps.
instructions: Sit on a bench with your legs apart and a dumbbell in one hand.
Rest the back of your upper arm against the inside of your thigh.
Curl the dumbbell toward your shoulder without moving your upper arm.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly to full extension.

name: Cross Body Hammer Curl
description: A hammer curl where the dumbbell travels across the body toward the opposite shoulder, emphasising the brachialis.
instructions: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing your thighs.
Curl one dumbbell across your body toward the opposite shoulder, keeping the neutral grip.
Lower slowly and repeat with the other arm.

name: Crunch (Cable)
description: The basic abdominal crunch, which flexes the spine to work the rectus abdominis.
instructions: Kneel in front of a high pulley with a rope attachment held beside your head.
Curl your torso by bringing your ribs toward your pelvis.
Squeeze your abs at the top, then return slowly without fully relaxing.

name: Crunch (Machine)
description: The basic abdominal crunch, which flexes the spine to work the rectus abdominis.
instructions: Sit at the ab crunch machine, grip the handles and place your feet under the pads.
Curl your torso by bringing your ribs toward your pelvis.
Squeeze your abs at the top, then return slowly without fully relaxing.

name: Crunch (Plate Loaded)
description: The basic abdominal crunch, which flexes the spine to work the rectus abdominis.
instructions: Sit at the plate-loaded crunch machine and grip the handles.
Curl your torso by bringing your ribs toward your pelvis.
Squeeze your abs at the top, then return slowly without fully relaxing.

name: Crunch (Bodyweight)
description: The basic abdominal crunch, which flexes the spine to work the rectus abdominis.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent, feet flat and hands lightly beside your head.
Curl your torso by bringing your ribs toward your pelvis.
Squeeze your abs at the top, then return slowly without fully relaxing.

name: Crunch (Weighted)
description: A crunch performed holding a weight on the chest or behind the head to add resistance.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat.
Hold a weight plate or dumbbell against your chest.
Curl your torso up by bringing your ribs toward your pelvis.
Lower slowly with control.

name: Cycling (Stationary Bike)
description: Cycling outdoors or on a stationary bike, a low-impact cardio activity that mainly works the quads, glutes and calves.
instructions: Set the resistance of the stationary bike to a comfortable starting level.
Adjust the saddle so your knee is only slightly bent at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
Start at an easy pace for a few minutes to warm up.
Keep a steady cadence, pushing and pulling through the whole pedal stroke.
Cool down at an easy pace at the end.

name: Cycling (Outdoor)
description: Cycling outdoors or on a stationary bike, a low-impact cardio activity that mainly works the quads, glutes and calves.
instructions: Check your bike, helmet and route before you set off.
Adjust the saddle so your knee is only slightly bent at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
Start at an easy pace for a few minutes to warm up.
Keep a steady cadence, pushing and pulling through the whole pedal stroke.
Cool down at an easy pace at the end.

name: Cycling - Air Bike
description: Cycling on an air bike (fan bike) that combines arm and leg work, with resistance that rises the harder you push.
instructions: Adjust the seat so your knee is slightly bent at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
Hold the moving handles and start pedalling at an easy pace.
Push and pull the handles in rhythm with your legs.
For intervals, sprint all out for the work period, then pedal easily during the rest.

name: Dead Bug
description: A core stability exercise lying on the back, where opposite arm and leg extend while the lower back stays pressed to the floor.
instructions: Lie on your back with your arms pointing to the ceiling and your knees bent at 90 degrees above your hips.
Press your lower back into the floor.
Slowly extend one arm behind your head and the opposite leg toward the floor.
Return to the start and switch sides, keeping your back flat throughout.

name: Dead Hang
description: Hanging from a bar with straight arms, which builds grip strength and decompresses the shoulders.
instructions: Grip a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, hands about shoulder-width apart.
Lift your feet and hang with straight arms and relaxed legs.
Keep your shoulders slightly engaged rather than fully slumped.
Hold for the planned time, then step down carefully.

name: Deadlift (Band)
description: A hip hinge lift from the floor that builds the whole posterior chain: glutes, hamstrings, back and grip.
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart.
Stand on the middle of the band.
Hinge at the hips and bend your knees to grip the weight just outside your legs, back flat and chest up.
Brace your core and push the floor away, keeping the weight close to your legs.
Stand tall with your hips fully extended, then lower the weight under control the same way.

name: Deadlift (Barbell)
description: A hip hinge lift from the floor that builds the whole posterior chain: glutes, hamstrings, back and grip.
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart.
Roll the barbell over your mid-foot, close to your shins.
Hinge at the hips and bend your knees to grip the weight just outside your legs, back flat and chest up.
Brace your core and push the floor away, keeping the weight close to your legs.
Stand tall with your hips fully extended, then lower the weight under control the same way.

name: Deadlift (Dumbbell)
description: A hip hinge lift from the floor that builds the whole posterior chain: glutes, hamstrings, back and grip.
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart.
Place a dumbbell on each side of your feet.
Hinge at the hips and bend your knees to grip the weight just outside your legs, back flat and chest up.
Brace your core and push the floor away, keeping the weight close to your legs.
Stand tall with your hips fully extended, then lower the weight under control the same way.

name: Deadlift (Smith Machine)
description: A hip hinge lift from the floor that builds the whole posterior chain: glutes, hamstrings, back and grip.
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart.
Set the Smith machine bar at mid-shin height, close to your shins.
Hinge at the hips and bend your knees to grip the weight just outside your legs, back flat and chest up.
Brace your core and push the floor away, keeping the weight close to your legs.
Stand tall with your hips fully extended, then lower the weight under control the same way.

name: Deadlift (Sumo)
description: A deadlift with a wide stance and hands inside the knees, which shortens the range of motion and works more quads and adductors.
instructions: Stand with your feet wide and toes pointed out, the bar over your mid-foot.
Grip the bar with your hands inside your knees and push your knees out.
Keep your chest up and back flat, then push the floor away to stand up.
Lower the bar under control the same way.

name: Deadlift High Pull
description: An explosive pull from the floor up to chest height, linking the deadlift to an upright row, for power and the upper traps.
instructions: Set up as for a deadlift with a grip slightly wider than shoulder width.
Lift the bar explosively, extending your hips and knees.
Shrug and pull the bar up close to your body, elbows high, to chest height.
Lower the bar under control back to the floor.

name: Decline Crunch
description: A crunch performed on a decline bench, which increases the range of motion and the load on the abs.
instructions: Secure your feet under the pads of a decline bench and lie back.
Place your hands across your chest or lightly beside your head.
Curl your torso up toward your knees.
Lower slowly until your back is close to the bench.

name: Decline Crunch (Weighted)
description: A decline crunch performed holding a weight to add resistance.
instructions: Secure your feet under the pads of a decline bench and lie back.
Hold a weight plate or dumbbell against your chest.
Curl your torso up toward your knees.
Lower slowly until your back is close to the bench.

name: Decline Push Up
description: A push-up with the feet raised on a box or bench, which shifts more work to the upper chest and shoulders.
instructions: Place your feet on a bench or box and your hands on the floor slightly wider than your shoulders.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your chest toward the floor.
Push back up to straight arms.

name: Diamond Push Up
description: A push-up with the hands close together forming a diamond, emphasising the triceps.
instructions: Start in a push-up position with your hands together under your chest, thumbs and index fingers forming a diamond.
Keep your body in a straight line.
Lower your chest toward your hands, keeping your elbows close to your body.
Push back up to straight arms.

name: Dip (Seated, Machine)
description: A triceps dip performed on a seated machine with a guided path.
instructions: Adjust the seat, sit with your back against the pad and grip the handles at your sides.
Push the handles down until your arms are extended.
Return slowly until your elbows are bent to about 90 degrees.

name: Dip (Seated, Plate Loaded)
description: A triceps dip performed on a seated machine with a guided path.
instructions: Adjust the seat, sit with your back against the pad and grip the handles at your sides.
Push the handles down until your arms are extended.
Return slowly until your elbows are bent to about 90 degrees.

name: Downward Dog
description: A yoga pose in an inverted V shape that stretches the hamstrings, calves and shoulders.
instructions: Start on your hands and knees.
Tuck your toes and lift your hips up and back, straightening your legs as much as comfortable.
Press your hands into the floor and lengthen your spine.
Hold while breathing slowly, then lower your knees to the floor.

name: Drag Curl
description: A curl where the weight is dragged up along the torso with the elbows moving back, emphasising the biceps and limiting the front deltoids.
instructions: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand, arms extended and palms facing forward.
Curl the dumbbells up while dragging them along your torso, letting your elbows travel back.
Squeeze at the top, then lower along the same path.

name: Dragon Flag
description: An advanced core exercise where the body is lowered as a rigid plank while lying on a bench, holding on behind the head.
instructions: Lie on a bench and grip it behind your head.
Lift your whole body until only your upper back touches the bench, body straight.
Lower your body slowly as one rigid line, without bending at the hips.
Stop before your lower back arches, then raise back up.

name: Dragonfly
description: Another name for the dragon flag: a demanding core exercise where the body is lowered as a rigid line from the shoulders.
instructions: Lie on a bench and grip it firmly behind your head.
Raise your legs and hips until your body is vertical, resting on your upper back.
Lower your body slowly as one straight line.
Raise back up before your lower back arches; bend your knees to make it easier.

name: Dual Low Bicep Curl
description: A cable curl using two low pulleys at once, keeping constant tension on both biceps.
instructions: Set both pulleys low and stand between them, holding one handle in each hand.
Curl both handles up toward your shoulders, keeping your elbows by your sides.
Squeeze, then lower slowly to full extension.

name: Elbow to Knee
description: A crunch with rotation where the elbow is brought toward the opposite knee, working the obliques.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and hands lightly behind your head.
Crunch up while rotating to bring one elbow toward the opposite knee.
Lower back down and repeat on the other side.

name: Elliptical Trainer
description: A low-impact cardio machine that combines leg and arm movement.
instructions: Step onto the pedals and hold the moving handles.
Start at an easy resistance to warm up.
Push and pull with your arms while striding smoothly with your legs, keeping an upright posture.
Increase the resistance or pace for the main part of the session, then cool down.

name: Face Pull
description: A cable pull toward the face with a rope, which works the rear deltoids, upper back and rotator cuff.
instructions: Set a pulley at upper chest or face height and attach a rope.
Hold the rope with your palms facing each other and step back until there is tension.
Pull the rope toward your face, separating the ends and driving your elbows out and back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades, then return slowly.

name: Farmers Walk (Dumbbell)
description: A loaded carry where heavy weights are held at the sides while walking, building grip, traps and core stability.
instructions: Pick up a heavy weight in each hand with a neutral grip, standing tall.
Brace your core and keep your shoulders back.
Walk with short, controlled steps for the planned distance.
Set the weights down by bending your knees, keeping your back flat.

name: Farmers Walk (Kettlebell)
description: A loaded carry where heavy weights are held at the sides while walking, building grip, traps and core stability.
instructions: Pick up a heavy weight in each hand with a neutral grip, standing tall.
Brace your core and keep your shoulders back.
Walk with short, controlled steps for the planned distance.
Set the weights down by bending your knees, keeping your back flat.

name: Floor Press (Barbell)
description: A bench press performed lying on the floor, which limits the range of motion and focuses on the lockout and the triceps.
instructions: Lie on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat.
Grip the barbell, set in a rack just above your chest, slightly wider than shoulder width and unrack it.
Lower the weight until your upper arms touch the floor.
Pause briefly, then press back up to straight arms.

name: Floor Press (Dumbbell)
description: A bench press performed lying on the floor, which limits the range of motion and focuses on the lockout and the triceps.
instructions: Lie on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand above your chest.
Lower the weight until your upper arms touch the floor.
Pause briefly, then press back up to straight arms.

name: Flutter Kicks
description: A lying core exercise with small alternating up and down leg kicks, working the lower abs and hip flexors.
instructions: Lie on your back with your hands under your glutes.
Lift your legs a few inches off the floor and raise your head slightly.
Kick your legs up and down in small, quick alternating movements.
Keep your lower back pressed into the floor throughout.

name: Frog Jumps
description: A plyometric exercise of deep squat jumps forward, building leg power and conditioning.
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder width and squat down, touching the floor between your feet.
Jump forward as far as you can, swinging your arms.
Land softly back into the deep squat.
Repeat continuously for the planned number of jumps.

name: Frog Pumps
description: A glute bridge variation with the soles of the feet together and knees out, which isolates the glutes.
instructions: Lie on your back with the soles of your feet together and your knees falling out to the sides.
Place a dumbbell on your hips if you want to add load.
Squeeze your glutes to lift your hips off the floor.
Lower and repeat quickly, keeping the tension in your glutes.

name: Front Lever Hold (Bodyweight)
description: An advanced static gymnastic hold where the body is held horizontal under a bar with straight arms, demanding huge lat and core strength.
instructions: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip, arms straight.
Pull your shoulder blades down and back and press the bar toward your hips.
Raise your body until it is horizontal, facing the ceiling, as straight as possible.
Hold for the planned time; use a tuck or a band to make it easier.

name: Front Lever Hold (Band)
description: An advanced static gymnastic hold where the body is held horizontal under a bar with straight arms, demanding huge lat and core strength.
instructions: Loop a resistance band over the bar and place it around your hips or feet for assistance.
Hang from a bar with an overhand grip, arms straight.
Pull your shoulder blades down and back and press the bar toward your hips.
Raise your body until it is horizontal, facing the ceiling, as straight as possible.
Hold for the planned time; use a tuck or a band to make it easier.

name: Front Lever Raise (Bodyweight)
description: A dynamic version of the front lever where the body is raised to horizontal and lowered under control.
instructions: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip, arms straight.
Keeping your arms straight, pull your body up until it is horizontal.
Lower slowly back to a hang.
Use a tuck position or a band to make it easier.

name: Front Lever Raise (Band)
description: A dynamic version of the front lever where the body is raised to horizontal and lowered under control.
instructions: Loop a resistance band over the bar and place it around your hips or feet for assistance.
Hang from a bar with an overhand grip, arms straight.
Keeping your arms straight, pull your body up until it is horizontal.
Lower slowly back to a hang.
Use a tuck position or a band to make it easier.

name: Front Raise (Band)
description: A shoulder raise in front of the body that targets the front deltoids.
instructions: Stand on the band and hold one end in each hand.
Stand tall, arms extended in front of your thighs.
Raise the weight in front of you with straight arms (slight elbow bend) to shoulder height.
Lower slowly without swinging your torso.

name: Front Raise (Barbell)
description: A shoulder raise in front of the body that targets the front deltoids.
instructions: Stand tall, arms extended in front of your thighs.
Raise the weight in front of you with straight arms (slight elbow bend) to shoulder height.
Lower slowly without swinging your torso.

name: Front Raise (Cable)
description: A shoulder raise in front of the body that targets the front deltoids.
instructions: Stand facing away from a low pulley, holding the handle between your legs.
Stand tall, arms extended in front of your thighs.
Raise the weight in front of you with straight arms (slight elbow bend) to shoulder height.
Lower slowly without swinging your torso.

name: Front Raise (Dumbbell)
description: A shoulder raise in front of the body that targets the front deltoids.
instructions: Hold a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs.
Stand tall, arms extended in front of your thighs.
Raise the weight in front of you with straight arms (slight elbow bend) to shoulder height.
Lower slowly without swinging your torso.

name: Front Raise (Plate Loaded)
description: A shoulder raise in front of the body that targets the front deltoids.
instructions: Hold a weight plate with both hands at the 3 and 9 o'clock positions.
Stand tall, arms extended in front of your thighs.
Raise the weight in front of you with straight arms (slight elbow bend) to shoulder height.
Lower slowly without swinging your torso.

name: Front Raise (Suspension)
description: A front raise performed with suspension straps, where the body leans back and is pulled up by the arms.
instructions: Hold the handles in front of you and lean back with your body straight.
With straight arms, raise the handles overhead, pulling your body up.
Lower slowly back to the start, keeping your core tight.

name: Front Squat
description: A squat with the bar held on the front of the shoulders, which keeps the torso upright and emphasises the quads.
instructions: Rest the bar on the front of your shoulders with a clean grip or crossed arms, elbows high.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Squat down keeping your chest and elbows up.
Drive through your feet to stand back up.

name: Full Squat
description: A barbell squat taken to full depth (hips below the knees), working the glutes and quads over their whole range.
instructions: Place the bar on your upper back and stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Squat down until your hips are below your knees, keeping your chest up and heels down.
Drive back up without letting your knees cave in.

name: Glute Bridge
description: A hip extension lying on the back that strengthens the glutes and hamstrings.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat, close to your glutes.
Squeeze your glutes and lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly.

name: Glute Ham Raise
description: A demanding posterior chain exercise where the body is lowered and raised by the hamstrings, usually on a GHD bench.
instructions: Secure your feet on a glute-ham developer with your knees just behind the pad.
Start upright with your body straight.
Lower your torso forward slowly by extending your knees, keeping your hips straight.
Pull yourself back up using your hamstrings.

name: Glute Kickback (Cable)
description: A hip extension where one leg is pushed back against resistance, isolating the glutes.
instructions: Attach an ankle strap to a low pulley, face the machine and hold it for support.
Kick one leg back and up by squeezing your glute, keeping your back flat.
Pause at full extension, then return slowly; complete all reps before switching legs.

name: Glute Kickback (Machine)
description: A hip extension where one leg is pushed back against resistance, isolating the glutes.
instructions: Position yourself on the kickback machine with your foot against the platform.
Kick one leg back and up by squeezing your glute, keeping your back flat.
Pause at full extension, then return slowly; complete all reps before switching legs.

name: Glute Kickback (Plate Loaded)
description: A hip extension where one leg is pushed back against resistance, isolating the glutes.
instructions: Position yourself on the plate-loaded kickback machine with your foot against the platform.
Kick one leg back and up by squeezing your glute, keeping your back flat.
Pause at full extension, then return slowly; complete all reps before switching legs.

name: Glute Kickback on Floor
description: A kneeling bodyweight kickback that works the glutes.
instructions: Start on your hands and knees with your back flat.
Kick one leg back and up, knee bent or straight, squeezing your glute.
Lower without touching the floor and repeat; switch legs after the set.

name: Goblet Squat
description: A squat with a kettlebell or dumbbell held against the chest, which encourages an upright torso and good depth.
instructions: Hold a kettlebell by the horns against your chest.
Stand with your feet slightly wider than shoulder width, toes slightly out.
Squat down between your knees, keeping your chest up and elbows inside your knees.
Drive through your feet to stand back up.

name: Gorilla Row
description: An alternating kettlebell row from a wide, hinged stance, with one bell resting on the floor while the other is rowed.
instructions: Place two kettlebells between your feet and take a wide stance.
Hinge at the hips with a flat back and grip both handles.
Row one kettlebell to your hip while pressing the other into the floor.
Lower it and alternate sides.

name: Hack Squat (Barbell)
description: A squat with the body supported on a sliding sled or with the bar behind the legs, which emphasises the quads.
instructions: Hold a barbell behind your legs with an overhand grip, standing with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Lower until your thighs are about parallel to the platform or floor.
Drive back up through your whole foot without locking your knees hard.

name: Hack Squat (Machine)
description: A squat with the body supported on a sliding sled or with the bar behind the legs, which emphasises the quads.
instructions: Place your shoulders under the pads and your feet shoulder-width apart on the platform, then release the safety.
Lower until your thighs are about parallel to the platform or floor.
Drive back up through your whole foot without locking your knees hard.

name: Hack Squat (Plate Loaded)
description: A squat with the body supported on a sliding sled or with the bar behind the legs, which emphasises the quads.
instructions: Place your shoulders under the pads and your feet shoulder-width apart on the platform, then release the safety.
Lower until your thighs are about parallel to the platform or floor.
Drive back up through your whole foot without locking your knees hard.

name: Hack Squat (Reverse)
description: A hack squat performed facing the machine, which shifts the work toward the glutes and hamstrings.
instructions: Stand on the platform facing the machine with your chest against the pad and shoulders under the pads.
Release the safety and hinge slightly forward.
Lower until your thighs are about parallel to the platform.
Drive back up, squeezing your glutes at the top.

name: Hammer Curl (Band)
description: A curl with a neutral grip (palms facing each other) that works the brachialis and brachioradialis as well as the biceps.
instructions: Stand on the band and hold one end in each hand with a neutral grip.
Keep your palms facing each other and your elbows at your sides.
Curl the handles up toward your shoulders.
Lower slowly to full extension.

name: Hammer Curl (Cable)
description: A curl with a neutral grip (palms facing each other) that works the brachialis and brachioradialis as well as the biceps.
instructions: Attach a rope to a low pulley and hold one end in each hand.
Keep your palms facing each other and your elbows at your sides.
Curl the handles up toward your shoulders.
Lower slowly to full extension.

name: Hammer Curl (Machine)
description: A curl with a neutral grip (palms facing each other) that works the brachialis and brachioradialis as well as the biceps.
instructions: Sit at the curl machine using the neutral-grip handles.
Keep your palms facing each other and your elbows at your sides.
Curl the handles up toward your shoulders.
Lower slowly to full extension.

name: Hammer Curl (Plate Loaded)
description: A curl with a neutral grip (palms facing each other) that works the brachialis and brachioradialis as well as the biceps.
instructions: Sit at the plate-loaded curl machine using the neutral-grip handles.
Keep your palms facing each other and your elbows at your sides.
Curl the handles up toward your shoulders.
Lower slowly to full extension.

name: Hammer Curl (Seated Incline)
description: A hammer curl lying back on an incline bench, which stretches the arm at the bottom of the movement.
instructions: Lie back on a bench inclined to about 45 degrees, a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing each other.
Curl the dumbbells up without bringing your elbows forward.
Lower slowly to a full stretch.

name: Hammer Curl (Standing)
description: A standing dumbbell hammer curl with both arms or alternating.
instructions: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing your body.
Curl the dumbbells up, keeping the neutral grip and your elbows fixed.
Lower slowly to full extension.

name: Hamstring Leg Curl (Lying, Machine)
description: A lying leg curl machine exercise that isolates the hamstrings.
instructions: Lie face down on the machine with the pad just above your heels and your knees just off the bench.
Grip the handles and keep your hips pressed into the bench.
Curl your heels toward your glutes.
Lower slowly to almost straight legs.

name: Hamstring Leg Curl (Lying, Plate Loaded)
description: A lying leg curl machine exercise that isolates the hamstrings.
instructions: Lie face down on the machine with the pad just above your heels and your knees just off the bench.
Grip the handles and keep your hips pressed into the bench.
Curl your heels toward your glutes.
Lower slowly to almost straight legs.

name: Hamstring Leg Curl (Seated, Machine)
description: A seated leg curl machine exercise that isolates the hamstrings in a stretched hip position.
instructions: Sit in the machine with the lower pad behind your ankles and the thigh pad secured above your knees.
Curl your heels down and back as far as possible.
Return slowly to straight legs.

name: Hamstring Leg Curl (Seated, Plate Loaded)
description: A seated leg curl machine exercise that isolates the hamstrings in a stretched hip position.
instructions: Sit in the machine with the lower pad behind your ankles and the thigh pad secured above your knees.
Curl your heels down and back as far as possible.
Return slowly to straight legs.

name: Hamstring Leg Curl (Standing, Machine)
description: A single-leg standing leg curl on a machine.
instructions: Stand at the machine with the pad behind the ankle of your working leg and hold the handles.
Curl your heel toward your glute while keeping your thigh still.
Lower slowly, then switch legs after the set.

name: Hamstring Leg Curl (Standing, Plate Loaded)
description: A single-leg standing leg curl on a machine.
instructions: Stand at the machine with the pad behind the ankle of your working leg and hold the handles.
Curl your heel toward your glute while keeping your thigh still.
Lower slowly, then switch legs after the set.

name: Handstand Hold
description: A static inverted hold on the hands, usually against a wall, that builds shoulder strength and balance.
instructions: Place your hands on the floor shoulder-width apart, about a hand's length from a wall.
Kick up so your heels rest against the wall.
Push the floor away with straight arms and keep your body tight.
Hold for the planned time, then come down carefully one leg at a time.

name: Handstand Push Up
description: A vertical push-up in a handstand, usually against a wall, that works the shoulders and triceps.
instructions: Kick up into a handstand with your heels against a wall, hands shoulder-width apart.
Lower your head slowly toward the floor, elbows slightly forward.
Press back up to straight arms.
Use a pad under your head and progress from pike push-ups if needed.

name: Hanging Knee Raise
description: A hanging core exercise where the knees are pulled toward the chest, working the lower abs.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with straight arms.
Without swinging, raise your knees toward your chest by curling your pelvis.
Lower your legs slowly under control.

name: Hanging Leg Raise
description: A hanging core exercise where straight legs are raised to hip height or higher, strongly working the lower abs and hip flexors.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with straight arms and legs together.
Raise your straight legs in front of you to at least hip height.
Lower slowly without swinging.

name: Heel Taps
description: A lying oblique exercise where the hand reaches alternately toward each heel.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent, feet flat and arms by your sides.
Lift your shoulders slightly off the floor.
Reach to one side to touch your heel, then to the other, alternating.
Keep your shoulders off the floor throughout the set.

name: Hex Press
description: A dumbbell press with the dumbbells squeezed together throughout, which increases the inner chest contraction.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench holding two hexagonal dumbbells pressed together above your chest.
Lower them to your chest while squeezing them together.
Press back up, keeping the dumbbells in contact.

name: High Knee Skips
description: A skipping drill with high knee drive, used as a warm-up and to improve running mechanics.
instructions: Skip forward, driving one knee up to hip height on each skip.
Swing your opposite arm in rhythm with the leg.
Land on the balls of your feet and keep a tall posture.
Continue for the planned distance or time.

name: High Knees
description: A cardio drill of running in place while driving the knees up high.
instructions: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
Run in place, driving your knees up to hip height.
Pump your arms and stay on the balls of your feet.
Keep a fast pace for the planned time.

name: HIIT
description: High-intensity interval training: short bursts of hard effort alternated with short recovery periods.
instructions: Warm up for 5 to 10 minutes.
Alternate hard work intervals (for example 20 to 40 seconds) with easy recovery intervals.
Choose exercises you can do with good form when tired (bike, rower, burpees, jumps).
Repeat for the planned number of rounds, then cool down.

name: Hip Abduction (Machine)
description: A machine exercise where the legs are pushed outward, working the glute medius and other hip abductors.
instructions: Sit in the machine with the pads against the outside of your knees.
Push your knees outward as far as comfortable.
Pause, then return slowly without letting the weights touch.

name: Hip Abduction (Plate Loaded)
description: A machine exercise where the legs are pushed outward, working the glute medius and other hip abductors.
instructions: Sit in the machine with the pads against the outside of your knees.
Push your knees outward as far as comfortable.
Pause, then return slowly without letting the weights touch.

name: Hip Adduction (Machine)
description: A machine exercise where the legs are squeezed inward, working the inner thighs.
instructions: Sit in the machine with the pads against the inside of your knees, legs apart.
Squeeze your legs together.
Return slowly to the start without letting the weights touch.

name: Hip Adduction (Plate Loaded)
description: A machine exercise where the legs are squeezed inward, working the inner thighs.
instructions: Sit in the machine with the pads against the inside of your knees, legs apart.
Squeeze your legs together.
Return slowly to the start without letting the weights touch.

name: Hip Thrust (Barbell)
description: A hip extension with the upper back resting on a bench, one of the most effective exercises for the glutes.
instructions: Sit with your upper back against a bench and roll a padded barbell over your hips.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your body is straight from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top, keeping your chin tucked.
Lower your hips slowly and repeat.

name: Hip Thrust (Machine)
description: A hip extension with the upper back resting on a bench, one of the most effective exercises for the glutes.
instructions: Sit in the hip thrust machine with your back on the pad and the belt or pad over your hips.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your body is straight from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top, keeping your chin tucked.
Lower your hips slowly and repeat.

name: Hip Thrust (Plate Loaded)
description: A hip extension with the upper back resting on a bench, one of the most effective exercises for the glutes.
instructions: Sit in the plate-loaded hip thrust machine with the pad over your hips.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your body is straight from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top, keeping your chin tucked.
Lower your hips slowly and repeat.

name: Hip Thrust (Smith Machine)
description: A hip extension with the upper back resting on a bench, one of the most effective exercises for the glutes.
instructions: Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your body is straight from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top, keeping your chin tucked.
Lower your hips slowly and repeat.

name: Hip Thrust (Bodyweight)
description: A hip extension with the upper back resting on a bench, one of the most effective exercises for the glutes.
instructions: Sit with your upper back against a bench, knees bent and feet flat.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your body is straight from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top, keeping your chin tucked.
Lower your hips slowly and repeat.

name: Hollow Rock
description: A gymnastic core exercise where the body holds a hollow, banana-shaped position and rocks back and forth.
instructions: Lie on your back and press your lower back into the floor.
Lift your arms overhead and your legs off the floor, both straight, to form a shallow banana shape.
Keeping this shape rigid, rock back and forth from your upper back to your hips.
Bend your knees or bring your arms forward to make it easier.

name: Incline Push Ups
description: A push-up with the hands raised on a bench or box, an easier variation that emphasises the lower chest.
instructions: Place your hands on a bench or box slightly wider than your shoulders.
Walk your feet back until your body is in a straight line.
Lower your chest toward the edge of the bench.
Push back up to straight arms.

name: Inverted Row
description: A horizontal bodyweight row under a bar or rings, which works the upper back and biceps.
instructions: Set a bar at about waist height and lie under it.
Grip the bar slightly wider than your shoulders and hang with your body straight, heels on the floor.
Pull your chest to the bar, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Lower slowly to straight arms; bend your knees to make it easier.

name: Iso-Lateral High Row
description: A plate-loaded row from a high angle with independent arms, working the lats and upper back.
instructions: Adjust the seat so you can just reach the handles above you and secure your thighs under the pad.
Pull the handles down and back toward your chest, one arm or both.
Squeeze your back, then return slowly to a full stretch.

name: Iso-Lateral Low Row
description: A plate-loaded row from a low angle with independent arms, targeting the lats and mid back.
instructions: Sit with your chest against the pad and grip the low handles.
Pull the handles toward your hips, driving your elbows back.
Squeeze your back, then return slowly to a full stretch.

name: Iso-Lateral Row (Machine)
description: A chest-supported machine row with independent arms, working the mid back, lats and rear deltoids.
instructions: Adjust the seat so the handles are at chest level and place your chest against the pad.
Grip the handles and pull them back, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Return slowly to a full stretch, one arm or both.

name: Iso-Lateral Row (Plate Loaded)
description: A chest-supported machine row with independent arms, working the mid back, lats and rear deltoids.
instructions: Adjust the seat so the handles are at chest level and place your chest against the pad.
Grip the handles and pull them back, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Return slowly to a full stretch, one arm or both.

name: Jump Rope
description: Skipping rope, a cardio exercise that also improves coordination, footwork and calf endurance.
instructions: Hold the handles at hip height with the rope behind you.
Turn the rope with your wrists, not your arms.
Jump just high enough for the rope to pass, landing softly on the balls of your feet.
Keep a steady rhythm for the planned time.

name: Jump Shrug
description: An explosive Olympic lifting drill where the bar is lifted from the hang with a jump and a shrug, for hip power.
instructions: Hold the barbell at mid-thigh with a clean grip, standing tall.
Dip slightly by bending your hips and knees, keeping the bar close.
